question: True or false: from the face alone, people can tell a tennis player who just won a big point from one who lost?
answer: False. Aviezer, Trope and Todorov showed photos of players at the moment of winning or losing. With the face alone, people guessed at chance; with the body alone, they did well. A winning face pasted on a losing body read as despair. At peak intensity, joy and agony contort the face the same way.
move: When feelings run high, read the body and the moment, not just the face.
ask: When I judge how someone is taking news, am I reading only their face?
trap: Assuming intense emotion shows most clearly on the face.
reference: Aviezer, Trope & Todorov, Body cues, not facial expressions, discriminate between intense positive and negative emotions, Science, 2012
